title: Greedy Best-First on Dubai (Downtown) ⚡
description: Visualizing Greedy Best-First pathfinding on Dubai (Downtown)
ig_caption:
Greedy Best-First Search vs A*: Pathfinding Comparison — Why Greedy Best-First Search rushes toward the destination ⚡

In this Lisbon (Alfama) visualization, Greedy Best-First expands the node that looks closest to the goal using only a heuristic h(n) (typically straight-line distance). That means it ignores path cost so it can sprint into the “best-looking” corridor… even if it leads to a dead end or a longer overall route.

🔧 Mechanic breakdown (graph search):
• Priority = h(n) only ✅ (fast decisions)
• No guarantee of optimality ❌ (it can take a scenic trap)
• Compared to A*: A* uses f(n)=g(n)+h(n), balancing “where you’ve been” + “where you’re going”

Takeaway: If your heuristic is misleading, Greedy can look brilliant locally and fail globally.

Debate: In your pathfinding use-case, would you rather be fast-but-risky (Greedy) or slightly slower-but-consistent (A*)?
